Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 4 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of 74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission reductions will be achieved. This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB) Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield. For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit- Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue), community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building, participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners. The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis — EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species (including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological connectivity. 1.1 Unique Project Benefits Outcome or impact PROJECT DETAILS 2.1 Project Goals, Design and Long-Term Viability 2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB, G1.2) The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024– July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and land speculation along river corridors. The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG 4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957 ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario, landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use change. The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586), Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. The project crediting period spans 40 years, from 01 May 2023 to 30 April 2063. During this period, the average annual ERRs are estimated at 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year. The project implements a comprehensive set of activities organized around four pillars: (1) Forest protection and monitoring, including satellite-based surveillance using Landsat, Sentinel-2 and Planet imagery, PRODES/DETER real-time deforestation alerts, drone-based photogrammetry and LiDAR surveys, and community-based patrols conducted in partnership with Comunidade São Tomé do Mocambo; (2) Sustainable livelihoods and bioeconomy, supporting the collection, -- 10 of 81 -- CCB & VCS Project Description Template CCB Version 3.0, VCS Version 4.4 11 CCB v3.0, VCS v4.4 processing, and commercialization of non-timber forest products (NTFPs) including Brazil nuts (Bertholletia excelsa), açaí (Euterpe spp.), copaíba oil (Copaifera spp.), and andiroba (Carapa guianensis), leveraging the project proponent's 20-year supply chain connecting Amazon communities to international markets; (3) Community infrastructure and well-being, encompassing solar energy systems, water capture and treatment, internet connectivity, and improvements to community facilities; and (4) Capacity building and environmental education, including training in sustainable forest management, organic and fair trade certification, fire prevention, and biodiversity monitoring techniques. The project area is situated within the Amazon biome ecoregion of Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests (WWF classification), characterized by dense ombrophilous forest (terra firme), alluvial forests (várzea and igapó), and transitional vegetation zones. The region supports significant biodiversity, including species classified as Vulnerable, Endangered, or Critically Endangered by the IUCN, such as Harpia harpyja (Harpy Eagle, VU), Pteronura brasiliensis (Giant Otter, EN), Priodontes maximus (Giant Armadillo, VU), and Bertholletia excelsa (Brazil Nut, VU). By maintaining forest cover across the 36 properties, the project ensures the continuity of vital ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, watershed regulation, nutrient cycling, and habitat connectivity within a contiguous forest block. Monitoring is carried out through an integrated system combining remote sensing (satellite imagery at multiple resolutions, drone surveys, FIRMS fire alerts), ground-based verification (permanent forest inventory plots, biodiversity transects, camera traps), and community-based surveillance (monthly patrols, fire detection and response). This multi-layered approach ensures early detection of threats and supports adaptive management. Climate Objectives: Avoid planned deforestation across the APD area of approximately 14,95 hectares, preventing the release of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e over the 40-year crediting period (May 2023 – April 2063), representing an average estimated emission reductions of approximately 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year. Community Objectives: Improve livelihoods of riverine communities within the project zone through sustainable economic alternatives based on NTFP value chains, community infrastructure investments (solar energy, water systems, connectivity), capacity building, and equitable benefit-sharing of carbon credit revenues. Biodiversity Objectives: Protect habitat for threatened species and maintain ecological connectivity within the Amazon biome by preventing fragmentation, preserving High Conservation Value (HCV) areas, and implementing a comprehensive biodiversity monitoring program. Some methodologies may require project proponents to quantify emissions that occur prior to this date to account for all project or baseline emissions. The initial crediting period start date for the Marcondes REDD+ Project is 01 May 2023, which is consistent with the definition of the initial crediting period start date under the VCS Program and conforms to the criteria specified in the applied methodology. The project does not involve multiple project activities and implements a single REDD+ activity in a grouped project design aimed at avoiding planned deforestation (APD). Accordingly, the crediting period start date is established based on the earliest implementation of project activities undertaken to prevent planned deforestation. The selected date corresponds to the commencement of project implementation activities, including the execution of carbon credit agreements with participating landowners and the initiation of monitoring activities across properties located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha in the state of Amazonas. This date also determines the start of the first monitoring period, from which emission reductions are accounted for under the project. The applied methodology does not require quantification of emissions occurring prior to the crediting period start date; therefore, this provision is not applicable to the project. Further details on the project start date and commencement of implementation are provided in Section 2.1.10 of the PD.. Mean annual temperature is 26.3°C, with minimal seasonal variation (range: 24°C to 34°C). Annual precipitation ranges from 2,000 to 2,500 mm, distributed across two distinct seasons: the rainy season (December to May, with peak rainfall in March–April) and the dry season (June to November, with minimum rainfall in September–October). Relative humidity averages 80–90% throughout the year. The region occasionally experiences 'friagem' events (cold fronts from the south) that can temporarily reduce temperatures by 5–8°C. Hydrology The project area lies within the drainage basin of the Amazon River (right bank) and the Nhamundá River system. The Nhamundá River, a clear-water river originating in the highlands of Roraima, flows southward forming the natural boundary between the states of Amazonas and Pará before joining the Amazon. Its watershed encompasses a significant portion of the project properties. The hydrological regime is strongly seasonal, with annual flooding of the várzea areas between February and June (peak in May–June) and low-water levels from September to November. Water bodies within the project zone include the Amazon River main channel, the Nhamundá River and its tributaries, numerous igarapés (small forest streams), and seasonal and permanent lakes (lagos de várzea). These water systems are critical for local communities, supporting fishing, transportation, and domestic water supply. 1 SUMMARY OF PROJECT BENEFITS
The Marcondes Reducing Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+) Project
is an AFOLU initiative focused on Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD), spanning a total area of
74,783 hectares of Amazon rainforest across 36 rural properties in the municipalities of
Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil. The project's core objective is
to conserve approximately 14,957 hectares of dense ombrophilous forest that would otherwise
be legally converted to cattle pasture under the Brazilian Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). By
the end of the 40-year crediting period, an estimated 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e of net GHG emission
reductions will be achieved.
This project is developed in alignment with the Climate, Community, and Biodiversity (CCB)
Standards v3.1, ensuring measurable benefits across three critical areas. From a climate
perspective, the conservation of 74,783 hectares of standing forest maintains critical carbon
stocks (668.42 tCO₂e/ha) and preserves the hydrological functions of the Nhamundá River
basin, a clearwater tributary draining the southern Guiana Shield.
For local communities, the project delivers transformative benefits to the Comunidade
Tradicional São Tomé do Mocambo do Arari (~80 families, Parintins) through a formal Benefit-
Sharing Plan encompassing direct monetary benefits (participation in carbon credit revenue),
community infrastructure (sanitation, energy, communication), training and capacity building,
participatory forest monitoring with paid community guards, and cultural heritage support for
traditional artisanal ceramics. The 40%/60% benefit-sharing structure ensures 60% of carbon
revenues flow directly to the 36 participating landowners.
The project prioritizes biodiversity conservation within the Uatumã–Trombetas Moist Forests
ecoregion, harboring at least 10 globally threatened mammal species (including Inia geoffrensis
— EN, Pteronura brasiliensis — EN, Tapirus terrestris — VU), 250+ bird species, 300+ fish species
(including endemic taxa in the Nhamundá River), and threatened tree species (Swietenia
macrophylla — VU, Bertholletia excelsa — VU). Forest conservation preserves ecosystem functions
including nutrient cycling, carbon sequestration, watershed protection, and ecological
connectivity.

2.1.1 Summary Description of the Project (VCS, 3.2, 3.6, 3.10, 3.11, 3.13, 3.14; CCB,
G1.2)
The Marcondes REDD+ project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and
Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The project area lies within the Middle Amazon
basin, in the Nhamundá River watershed, a region of significant ecological value facing persistent
deforestation pressures. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality
retains approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land
area. Despite recent national progress, PRODES/INPE data shows Amazon deforestation
declined by 50% cumulatively between 2022 and 2025, reaching 5,796 km² in the August 2024–
July 2025 period the state of Amazonas remains the second-largest contributor to absolute
deforestation in the Legal Amazon, with 1,016 km² cleared in the most recent PRODES cycle. The
main drivers of deforestation in the project region include legal land clearance for cattle ranching
and agriculture, selective and illegal logging, and pressure from infrastructure development and
land speculation along river corridors.
The Marcondes REDD+ project aims to avoid planned deforestation and degradation across a
total project area of approximately 74,783 hectares (per GIS measurement, SIRGAS 2000 – EPSG
4674), comprising 36 rural properties (fazendas) held by approximately 24 landowners and
entities. As an Avoided Planned Deforestation (APD) project under VM0007 v1.8, the project
prevents the legally authorized conversion of 20% of each property's area (approximately 14,957
ha total APD area) from dense ombrophilous forest to cattle pasture. Under the baseline scenario,
landowners would legally convert these forest areas to cattle pasture in accordance with the
Brazilian Forest Code, resulting in significant carbon emissions from forest clearing and land-use
change.
The project is located in the municipalities of Nhamundá (pop. 20,136, IBGE 2022; IDHM 0.586),
Parintins (pop. 96,251), and Barreirinha, in the state of Amazonas, Brazil. The total estimated
emission reductions and removals (ERRs) generated during the crediting period are
10,008,517.90 tCO₂e. The project crediting period spans 40 years, from 01 May 2023 to 30 April
2063. During this period, the average annual ERRs are estimated at 250,212.95 tCO₂e per year.
The project implements a comprehensive set of activities organized around four pillars: (1) Forest
protection and monitoring, including satellite-based surveillance using Landsat, Sentinel-2 and
Planet imagery, PRODES/DETER real-time deforestation alerts, drone-based photogrammetry
and LiDAR surveys, and community-based patrols conducted in partnership with Comunidade
São Tomé do Mocambo; (2) Sustainable livelihoods and bioeconomy, supporting the collection,

(Bertholletia excelsa), açaí (Euterpe spp.), copaíba oil (Copaifera spp.), and andiroba (Carapa
guianensis), leveraging the project proponent's 20-year supply chain connecting Amazon
communities to international markets; (3) Community infrastructure and well-being,
encompassing solar energy systems, water capture and treatment, internet connectivity, and

The project area is situated within the Amazon biome ecoregion of Uatumã–Trombetas Moist
Forests (WWF classification), characterized by dense ombrophilous forest (terra firme), alluvial
forests (várzea and igapó), and transitional vegetation zones. The region supports significant
biodiversity, including species classified as Vulnerable, Endangered, or Critically Endangered by
the IUCN, such as Harpia harpyja (Harpy Eagle, VU), Pteronura brasiliensis (Giant Otter, EN),
Priodontes maximus (Giant Armadillo, VU), and Bertholletia excelsa (Brazil Nut, VU). By
maintaining forest cover across the 36 properties, the project ensures the continuity of vital
ecosystem services including carbon sequestration, watershed regulation, nutrient cycling, and
habitat connectivity within a contiguous forest block.
Monitoring is carried out through an integrated system combining remote sensing (satellite
imagery at multiple resolutions, drone surveys, FIRMS fire alerts), ground-based verification
(permanent forest inventory plots, biodiversity transects, camera traps), and community-based
surveillance (monthly patrols, fire detection and response). This multi-layered approach ensures
early detection of threats and supports adaptive management.
Climate Objectives:
Avoid planned deforestation across the APD area of approximately 14,95 hectares, preventing
the release of 10,008,517.90 tCO₂e over the 40-year crediting period (May 2023 – April 2063),
representing an average estimated emission reductions of approximately 250,212.95 tCO₂e per
year.
Community Objectives:
Improve livelihoods of riverine communities within the project zone through sustainable
economic alternatives based on NTFP value chains, community infrastructure investments (solar
energy, water systems, connectivity), capacity building, and equitable benefit-sharing of carbon
credit revenues.
Biodiversity Objectives:
Protect habitat for threatened species and maintain ecological connectivity within the Amazon
biome by preventing fragmentation, preserving High Conservation Value (HCV) areas, and
implementing a comprehensive biodiversity monitoring program. The project is not located within
a jurisdiction covered by a jurisdictional REDD+ program.

Land ownership and tenure of the Marcondes REDD+ project properties are governed by applicable
federal and state legislation in Brazil, which establishes the legal basis for possession,
environmental registration, georeferenced boundary certification, and formal land tenure rights.
Federal Legislation
▪ Brazilian Civil Code (Law No. 10.406/2002, Articles 1.196–1.228): Recognizes possession
(posse) as a protected right and establishes usucapião as a legal pathway to ownership.
▪ Brazilian Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012): Establishes the requirement for Cadastro
Ambiental Rural (CAR) registration and mandates an 80% Legal Reserve for rural properties
located in the Legal Amazon.
▪ Law No. 10.267/2001 and Decree No. 4.449/2002: Establish the SIGEF system (Sistema de
Gestão Fundiária) and define requirements for georeferenced rural property registration.
▪ Law No. 6.015/1973 (Public Registries Law): Regulates property registration and the Matrícula
system at the Cartório de Registro de Imóveis.
State Legislation (Amazonas)
▪ State Law No. 2.665/2001: Regulates state land policy, including the issuance of Concessão
de Direito Real de Uso (CDRU) for state lands and terras devolutas.
▪ State Law No. 3.135/2007: Establishes the Amazonas State Policy on Climate Change,
providing the legal framework for carbon credit projects and ecosystem services.
Land Ownership
The Marcondes REDD+ project is a grouped project and for validation comprises 36 rural properties
located primarily in the municipality of Nhamundá, Parintins and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas,
Brazil. The total project area is approximately 74,698 hectares, held by approximately 24
landowners and legal entities.
All 36 project properties are registered in the SIGEF system (Sistema de Gestão Fundiária)
managed by INCRA, providing legally recognized, georeferenced, non-overlapping property
boundaries. All properties are also registered in the Cadastro Ambiental Rural (CAR), which includes
declared georeferenced boundaries, identification of Permanent Protection Areas (APPs), and
demarcation of Legal Reserves in accordance with the 80% requirement applicable in the Legal
Amazon. Applications for Concessão de Direito Real de Uso (CDRU) have been submitted to the

General Location and Access
The Marcondes REDD+ project covers approximately 74,698 hectares across 36 rural properties
primarily in the municipality of Nhamundá (14,107 km², Baixo Amazonas sub-region), with

Geology, Geomorphology and Topography
The project area is situated within the Amazon Sedimentary Basin, underlain by Cretaceous and
Tertiary sedimentary formations. The predominant geological unit is the Alter do Chão Formation
(Cretaceous–Paleogene), composed of sandstones, siltstones, and claystones, typical of the
central Amazon lowlands. Geomorphologically, the landscape comprises dissected tertiary
plateaus (terra firme), fluvial terraces, and extensive floodplain systems (várzea) along the
Amazon and Nhamundá rivers. Topography is gently undulating to flat, with elevations generally
between 30 m and 120 m in the terra firme zones. The Nhamundá River, which forms the
boundary between the states of Amazonas and Pará, has a sandy bed and clear waters, with
several rapids in its upper course and lake formations at the confluence with the Paracatu River.

Climate
The climate is classified as Equatorial Humid (Af in the Köppen system), controlled by the
Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) and equatorial continental air masses. Mean annual
temperature is 26.3°C, with minimal seasonal variation (range: 24°C to 34°C). Annual
precipitation ranges from 2,000 to 2,500 mm, distributed across two distinct seasons: the rainy
season (December to May, with peak rainfall in March–April) and the dry season (June to
November, with minimum rainfall in September–October). Relative humidity averages 80–90%
throughout the year. The region occasionally experiences 'friagem' events (cold fronts from the
south) that can temporarily reduce temperatures by 5–8°C.
Hydrology
The project area lies within the drainage basin of the Amazon River (right bank) and the
Nhamundá River system. The Nhamundá River, a clear-water river originating in the highlands of
Roraima, flows southward forming the natural boundary between the states of Amazonas and
Pará before joining the Amazon. Its watershed encompasses a significant portion of the project
properties. The hydrological regime is strongly seasonal, with annual flooding of the várzea areas
between February and June (peak in May–June) and low-water levels from September to
November. Water bodies within the project zone include the Amazon River main channel, the
Nhamundá River and its tributaries, numerous igarapés (small forest streams), and seasonal and
permanent lakes (lagos de várzea). These water systems are critical for local communities,
supporting fishing, transportation, and domestic water supply.

Soils (Pedology)
Soils in the project area are predominantly Dystrophic Yellow Latosols (Oxisols) in the terra firme
zones, characterized by deep, well-drained profiles with low natural fertility, high aluminum
saturation, and acidic pH (4.0–5.5). In the várzea zones, Gleysols and Fluvic Neosols
predominate, with higher fertility due to annual sediment deposition from the Amazon River.
Podzols (Spodosols) occur in localized areas of white-sand formations (campinarana). The low
natural fertility of terra firme soils is a key factor limiting agricultural productivity and reinforcing
the economic incentive for forest conversion to extensive cattle pasture the principal
deforestation driver in the project region.

The project area is covered predominantly by Dense Ombrophilous Forest (Floresta Ombrófila
Densa) in the terra firme zones, with Alluvial Ombrophilous Forest (várzea and igapó) along the
river corridors. According to Global Forest Watch (2020), Nhamundá municipality retains
approximately 1.26 million hectares of natural forest, covering roughly 89% of its land area. The

seasonally flooded alluvial forest along the Amazon and Nhamundá rivers, with lower canopy

Deforestation Dynamics
Deforestation in the Brazilian Legal Amazon reached 5,796 km² in the August 2024–July 2025
PRODES/INPE cycle, representing an 11.08% decrease from the prior period and the third-lowest
rate since measurements began in 1988. This marks the third consecutive year of decline under
the Lula administration, with a cumulative 50% reduction compared to 2022. The state of
Amazonas specifically recorded a 16.93% reduction in deforestation (to approximately 1,000
km²). However, forest degradation has increased significantly 2,500,000+ hectares degraded in
2024, a 163% increase compared to 2022, primarily due to fire. Despite declining national rates,
private landowners in the Baixo Amazonas sub-region continue to exercise their legal right to
convert up to 20% of property area under the Forest Code (Law 12.651/2012). The Marcondes
project addresses this ongoing baseline threat on 36 specific properties where deforestation
authorization has been sought from IPAAM. Nhamundá municipality (14,107.5 km², pop. 20,136,
IBGE 2022; pop. estimated 21,251 in 2025; IDHM 0.586) has 62 rural communities and limited
economic alternatives to livestock, reinforcing the economic rationale for planned forest
conversion.

Municipality Overview - Nhamundá
Nhamundá: Population 20,136 (IBGE Census 2022), estimated at 21,251 (2025). Area: 14,107

livelihood diversification programs. Specific interventions include: installation of solar energy

development to diversify income sources beyond subsistence agriculture.

2.2 Without-project Land Use Scenario and Additionality
2.2.1 Conditions Prior to Project Initiation and Land Use Scenarios without the Project
(VCS, 3.13; CCB, G2.1)
The following scenarios represent the range of possible land-use outcomes in the absence of the
Marcondes REDD+ project. These scenarios were developed based on analysis of regional land-
use dynamics, landowner intentions, legal frameworks, and historical deforestation patterns in the
municipalities of Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha, State of Amazonas, Brazil.
SCENARIO 1: Maintenance of forest cover (conservation without project)
Maintenance of the forest cover of 20% of the property, where land use conversion is allowed by
law: the area is maintained without economic activities or conservation measures, but exposed to
invasions and illegal deforestation, antecedents to livestock a common practice in the region. The
landowner remains responsible for taxes to maintain ownership.

SCENARIO 2: Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (APD)
Legal deforestation of 20% of the property (deforestation with allowances), where land use
conversion is allowed by law, i.e., forest suppression for pasture (livestock). Under the Brazilian
Forest Code (Law No. 12.651/2012), rural properties in the Legal Amazon must maintain an 80%
Legal Reserve, meaning up to 20% may be legally converted.
SCENARIO 3: Illegal deforestation exceeding 20%
Illegal deforestation of over 20% of the property (deforestation without a grant), where the
conversion of land use exceeds the legal limit, driven by pasture expansion, agricultural purposes,
or real estate speculation.
Evidence of deforestation drivers in the project area includes: (a) all 36 property owners hold
environmental license applications (ASV) filed with IPAAM, demonstrating documented intent to
clear the legally convertible 20% of their properties for pasture establishment; (b) PRODES/INPE
and MapBiomas historical data show progressive deforestation on comparable private properties
in the Nhamundá, Parintins, and Barreirinha municipalities; (c) the Nhamundá municipal economy
is dominated by cattle ranching and subsistence agriculture (IBGE Municipal Agricultural
Production data), with limited economic alternatives; (d) pasture land/agriculture land values
exceed forest land values in the region, providing direct economic incentive for conversion; (e) road
access improvements and population growth (4.82% increase from 2022 to 2024 per IBGE) are
increasing pressure on forested lands.
2.2.2 Most-Likely Scenario Justification (CCB, G2.1)
The most likely scenario observed for the Marcondes project area is the conversion of land use
and land cover from forest to livestock areas, legally (APD). Legal deforestation of 20% of the
property (Scenario 2) is considered the most plausible baseline scenario because the land is
expected to be converted to non-forest land and the conversion is legally authorized and
documented, following VM0007 v1.8.
The identified deforestation agents are the landowners themselves, who have documented legal
authorization to clear up to 20% of their property areas under the Forest Code (Law
12.651/2012). Evidence includes: (a) IPAAM environmental license applications (ASV) filed by all
36 property holders; (b) property registration in SIGEF demonstrating legal control of the land; (c)
CAR (Cadastro Ambiental Rural) registration identifying the legal reserve and APD-eligible areas;
(d) economic profile consistent with agricultural expansion the landowners include individual
farmers, family groups (e.g., Fazenda AnaLina I/II/III, Fazenda Irmãos Marcondes, Fazenda André
Marcondes IV/V), and corporate entities (FIEMU Corporation, Marcondes Q Corporation) whose
primary economic activity is or would be cattle ranching.

In the absence of the Marcondes REDD+ project, neither the community benefits nor the
biodiversity conservation outcomes would occur. The project area is located in a region of the
